title: add-log-heft-index-and-cost-provenance-playground
author: Oliver Grant
description: Introduce a lightweight "log_heft_index" metric and an interactive Cost Provenance Playground to help SREs and engineers correlate verbose logging with unexpected token-level inference cost. Motivation: while we have token-cost and span telemetry, teams struggle to attribute cost spikes to excessive logging or chat-system debug output that inflates prompt/response sizes. This PR adds: 1) a runtime-exposed metric (redwood_runtime.log_heft) that weights log lines by verbosity and semantic size; 2) trace/span enrichment to annotate invocation traces with log_heft and primary provenance keys so traces can be joined with log shards; 3) a Console dashboard (Cost Provenance Playground) with panels: log-heft scatter vs token-cost, session provenance sankey, provenance query builder, and an interactive sample explorer that links to a sampled trace and compact log excerpt; 4) an alert tuning change: new alert rule heavy-log-cost-drift that triggers only when log_heft > P95 and cost-delta exceeds a dynamic window, plus a suppressor to reduce noisy alerts from known high-verbosity clients; 5) sampling adjustment: span sampler gets a small prioritization boost for invocations with high log_heft so we preserve observability for potential cost-root causes; 6) tests and a small synthetic replaybench to validate provenance joins at scale. Backwards compatibility: metric addition is additive-only; no breaking API changes. Implementation notes: log_heft is computed at log-emit time in the runtime library using a heuristic combining token-estimate, structured field count, and message nesting depth; the trace enricher attaches these as tags and emits a compact provenance key derived from the invocation fingerprint and KV-cache-id. The Console JSON is intentionally lightweight to allow iterative refinement by SREs. See linked Linear tasks for follow-up instrumentation and threshold tuning.
